title: Anti-fascist march and clashes with far-right group in Gorizia

tea.why: Organised by anti-fascist groups, protesters marched through Gorizia while encountering members of the far-right group CasaPound.
tea.want: Protesters demanded the closure of all fascist headquarters in the region.
tea.changed: Nov 7, 2026: Clashes occurred when far-right members tried to break a police blockade, resulting in three injured police officers.

summary: An anti-fascist march took place in Gorizia, organized by the Collettivo Giovani Antifa. Approximately 200 participants walked through the city under heavy rain while demanding the closure of all fascist headquarters in the region. Tensions arose when the procession passed near the headquarters of the far-right movement CasaPound in Via Mazzini, which was sealed off by riot police. According to news reports, members of CasaPound and Blocco studentesco exchanged insults with the marchers and attempted to break through police lines to reach the demonstrators. Police intervened to contain the push, resulting in three officers sustaining injuries, including one who suffered a shoulder dislocation with a 21-day prognosis. Despite the confrontations near the blockaded street, the main anti-fascist march continued along its route.
demands: Closure of all fascist headquarters in the region
response: Police established a blockade with riot gear, shields, helmets, and batons in Via Mazzini to separate the groups, and intervened when far-right individuals attempted to breach the line.

updates.text: An anti-fascist march of about 200 people took place in Gorizia under heavy rain, organized by Collettivo Giovani Antifa.
Far-right CasaPound and Blocco studentesco members gathered near Via Mazzini, where police formed a blockade.
Clashes erupted when far-right individuals attempted to break the police blockade to confront the marchers, injuring three officers.
